_comment: Symbol-index source configuration. Paths are candidate lists: the first
existing entry wins. Every build records the resolved paths and their
SHA-256s into the database meta table, so an index is always
reproducible/auditable regardless of which candidate was used.
Override with: python tools/symbols/rustcraft_symbols.py build --sources FILE

artifacts.name: Minecraft 1.12.2 dedicated server (notch)
artifacts.note: Server jar as distributed; bundled libraries are excluded by the mc entry filter (mapping universe).

artifacts.name: Minecraft 1.12.2 client (notch)
artifacts.note: Client-only classes absent from the server jar; also makes FORGE_PATCHED (merged jar) fully comparable.

artifacts.name: Forge 14.23.5.2847 binpatched merged jar (notch)
artifacts.note: Vanilla bytes + Forge binary patches. Per-method code hashes compare against VANILLA_NOTCH to expose what Forge changed.

artifacts.name: Forge 14.23.5.2864 recompiled, MCP snapshot 20171003 naming
artifacts.note: Human-readable MCP names. Recompiled from patched sources: code hashes are NOT comparable to runtime jars; use FORGE_PATCHED for byte-level diffing.

artifacts.name: Runtime-transformed class dump (sc-bisect-obs campaign)
artifacts.note: Classes as the live LaunchClassLoader actually defined them (SRG names, post-transform bytecode). Runtime was Forge 14.23.5.2860 with the Target C mod set, so live bytes = vanilla + Forge-2860 runtime-applied binary patches + mod coremods. Partial coverage: only classes dumped by that campaign. Machine-local, under target/.
